summary: This is a real, buildable, fairly complete RA2 + Yuri's Revenge skirmish engine. It is the most feature-rich descendant of the reconstructed Chrono Divide TypeScript client: TypeScript, React 19, Vite 8 and Three.js r183 on WebGL2, with Tauri 2, Android and iOS shells. The lineage is Chrono Divide client -> huangkaoya/redalert2 @8c07f10 -> ammaarreshi/RedAlert2-Mac-iOS-iPad (63 commits) -> StillM8 (about 306 commits on main and about 600 on beta, mostly AI-agent work: 170 commits on 2026-08-11 alone). It adds to the huangkaoya base: YR, a much stronger skirmish bot, save/load, WebRTC LAN, an Ares/Mental Omega compatibility layer and a Bink menu-video decoder. Verified locally: main installs, builds in about 1 s and passes 513/513 tests, but fails its own typecheck with 68 errors. beta installs, builds, passes 858/858 tests and typechecks clean. There is no campaign, no online play and no map editor. The licensing is the main problem. The GPL-3.0 grant it relies on has been disclaimed by its own upstream: on 2026-09-03 huangkaoya replaced the GPL LICENSE with a notice saying the repo holds "code reconstructed from the Chrono Divide client", which "is not licensed under GPL-3.0 or any other open-source license". StillM8 still ships GPL-3.0 and its own notices admit the grant is "unverified". The renderer is a strong technical base for a 2.5D HD upgrade: a real 3D scene with an isometric orthographic camera, voxels as real meshes with shadow maps, and an event-driven FX layer. Legally, though, it is only defensible for private, non-commercial experimentation. license_evidence:
VERIFIED in the clone and via the API:
(1) The root LICENSE and redalert2/LICENSE are the full GPL-3.0 text, and the GitHub API reports spdx_id "GPL-3.0". redalert2/package.json has no "license" field and is "private": true.

(2) THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md makes these admissions itself:
- The engine is "Vendored from huangkaoya/redalert2 at commit 8c07f10, which publishes under GPL-3.0".
- It says "Chrono Divide's game client has never been open-sourced by its author" and "the GPL-3.0 grant this repository relies on is **unverified**".
- It also says "If Alexandru Ciucă objects, this repository comes down."
- The skirmish AI (src/game/ai/thirdpartbot/**) is "Derived from Supalosa's Chrono Divide bot" and "**No licence is declared.**" The API confirms Supalosa/supalosa-chronodivide-bot has license null.

(3) AI-USE.md says the engine itself, "roughly 127,000 lines, is not AI-written. It is Chrono Divide's, via RA2WEB and huangkaoya".

(4) KEY NEW FACT, VERIFIED in the git history of huangkaoya/ts-redalert2 (huangkaoya/redalert2 now redirects there). Commit 898d891 (2026-09-03, "Revise LICENSE to reflect copyright holder's terms") replaced the GPL text with a notice. That notice says the repo "contains code reconstructed from the Chrono Divide client", that "The Chrono Divide copyright holder has not licensed Chrono Divide-derived material", and that "Such material is not licensed under GPL-3.0 or any other open-source license." The GitHub API now reports that upstream's license as NOASSERTION. Its README already said all rights "belong to the owner of Chronodivide" and prohibited commercial use.

StillM8 last pushed on 2026-09-08 and has not updated its notices, which now misstate the upstream license.

(5) Retail-content history. Earlier commits carried EA data that was later removed: redalert2/public/ini.mix (retail rules/art/ai INIs, removed in cf899d4), and 10 Westwood files inside ra2cd.mix (stripped in fca65f8). A fork carries that history.
provenance: Derived from the reconstructed Chrono Divide proprietary client, via RA2WEB -> huangkaoya/redalert2 @8c07f10 -> ammaarreshi/RedAlert2-Mac-iOS-iPad -> StillM8. It is not a GitHub fork: it is a copy of ammaarreshi's full history plus StillM8's commits. About 76% of the inherited engine files are byte-identical to huangkaoya's.

Its message says "Base: huangkaoya/redalert2 @ 8c07f10" and calls it the "Chronodivide-lineage RA2 TypeScript engine". Commit 991945d is the current HEAD of ammaarreshi/RedAlert2-Mac-iOS-iPad. - servers.ini says "must not point at Chrono Divide's production servers" and pins gameVersion=0.65.1 (a CD client version).
- The credits fallback reads "Original Project Development\tChronodivide".
- Upstream now says outright that it is "code reconstructed from the Chrono Divide client".

(e) docs/PORTING_PLAYBOOK.md: "What we have is a *reconstruction*: Chronodivide ... reverse-engineered".

(f) Authors: StillM8 has 366 commits plus 197 as "Muhammad <stillm8mail@gmail.com>" (the same person, whose profile bio reads "Driven by AI"). Ammaar Reshi has 63 plus 1, and github-actions 26. AI-USE.md credits Claude, Gemini and GPT with most of the non-engine code.
tech_stack:
- TypeScript 5.9.3 with React 19.2.4 for the DOM UI.
- Vite 8.0.1 (rolldown) and Bun 1.3.10, pinned via the packageManager field. Bun 1.3.14 was used locally.
- three 0.183.2 (WebGLRenderer, so WebGL2 only) with three.meshline 1.4.0 and shader-particle-engine 1.0.6, which needs a THREE global via setupThreeGlobal.ts.
- 7z-wasm; @ffmpeg/ffmpeg 0.12 for in-browser import and transcoding; @ra2web/pcxfile and @ra2web/wavefile.
- mersenne-twister for the deterministic PRNG; Playwright 1.58 for the debug:* flows.
- Tauri 2.11 desktop shell (redalert2/src-tauri, Rust), Kotlin/WebView Android shell, Swift/WKWebView iOS shell (XcodeGen).
- A Rust Bink v1 decoder compiled to WASM (wasm/bink-decoder, prebuilt at public/bink/bink_decoder.wasm).
- Code size: about 170k lines of TS on main and about 189k on beta.
- Structure: src/game (simulation, about 61k lines on beta), src/engine (rendering, audio, resources, about 28k), src/gui (about 38k), src/data (file formats, about 7.5k), src/extensions/ares (about 12k on beta), src/network (about 4.6k), src/test (about 23k on beta).
renderer_architecture:
Everything below is VERIFIED in code unless marked otherwise.

**Scene, camera and lighting setup**
- A true 3D Three.js scene with an OrthographicCamera. WorldScene.createCamera sets rotation order YXZ, rotation.y=+ISO_CAMERA_BETA and rotation.x=-ISO_CAMERA_ALPHA, which reproduces the 2.5D isometric view.
- Renderer.ts wraps a single THREE.WebGLRenderer with shadowMap enabled, NoToneMapping and SRGB output.
- The pixel ratio is clamped to 0.5–3, and native device-pixel rendering was added upstream in 524221c.
- Scenes (world and UI) are rendered sequentially per viewport in Renderer.render(). The UI is a separate UiScene with its own ortho camera.
- The world has an AmbientLight at 0.8 plus one DirectionalLight at a fixed LIGHT_OFFSET.
- The shadow ortho box is fitted to the visible area. The shadow map is up to 8192² on desktop and 1024² on touch devices.

**Asset decoding (src/data/)**
- MixFile, IdxFile, AudioBagFile, ShpFile, TmpFile, VxlFile, HvaFile, Palette, PcxFile, CsfFile, IniParser and MapFile.
- A VirtualFileSystem mounts the MIX archives. Imports go into OPFS via GameResImporter, using 7z-wasm and ffmpeg.

**SHP sprites**
- ShpTextureAtlas packs each frame as an IndexedBitmap into TextureAtlas, which is an R8 THREE.DataTexture (RedFormat).
- ShpBuilder and BatchShpBuilder create sprite quads (SpriteUtils.createSpriteGeometry) facing the camera.
- The material is PaletteBasicMaterial, a MeshBasicMaterial whose shader chunks are patched with paletteShaderLib. The fragment shader reads the palette index from .r and looks it up in a palette texture row. The row is chosen per instance or per vertex (instancePaletteOffset / vertexPaletteOffset), which is how house-color remap palettes are handled.
- Lighting is multiplied in the palette's byte domain (extraLight, vertexColorMult). The colorspace chunk is replaced, with the comment "Safe only while nothing renders a palette material into a WebGLRenderTarget".

**TMP terrain**
- MapTileLayer.createTileObjects draws every tile's TmpDrawable into one R8 atlas.
- Each tile becomes a sprite quad positioned by Coords.tile3dToWorld, so tile heights sit in real 3D.
- All tiles are merged into ONE mesh with a per-vertex vertexColorMult carrying per-tile lighting from Lighting.compute(LightingType.Full, tile).

**VXL/HVA voxels**
- Voxels are turned into real meshes by VxlGeometryNaiveBuilder, VxlGeometryCulledBuilder and VxlGeometryMonotoneBuilder (greedy/monotone meshing), pooled in VxlGeometryPool.
- VxlBuilder applies the HVA section transforms. The materials are PaletteLambert and PalettePhong.
- paletteFullLightFragment replaces Phong with the retail formula (0.8 + 1.3·dotNL) × cell light, diffuse only.
- Voxels cast and receive real shadow maps.
- VxlBuilderFactory picks VxlBatchedBuilder when Renderer.supportsInstancing() is true. That function checks the WebGL1 extension 'ANGLE_instanced_arrays'. INFERENCE (not run in a browser): WebGL2 contexts do not expose that extension, so three r183 returns null and instancing is probably always off.

**Lighting, effects and particles**
- Lighting.ts and LightingDirector apply map [Lighting] ambient/RGB and superweapon flashes (NukeLightingFx, LightningStormFx), plus per-tile lamp lights.
- Shroud and fog use MapShroudLayer with premultiplied MultiplyBlending.
- Effects include TeslaFx, LaserFx, RadBeamFx and MindControlLinkFx (MeshLine).
- Particles use the old shader-particle-engine (DamageSmokeFx, TrailerSmokeFx, SparkFx). Explosions are SHP animations spawned by WarheadDetonateFxHandler in response to game events.
- There is no weather or water shader. Water is just TMP tiles; ShipWakeTrailPlugin adds wakes.

**Simulation, networking, audio and video**
- The simulation in src/game is deterministic lockstep. It imports three only for math and never imports the renderer: 0 imports of engine/renderable or engine/gfx from game/.
- LAN uses WebRTC with manual SDP/QR exchange (network/lan/LanLockstepTurnManager.ts, ManualSdpLanSession.ts, LanMeshSession.ts).
- The WOL/IRC online code remains, but servers.ini endpoints are blank.
- Audio uses Web Audio (engine/sound: Mixer, Eva, Music, WorldSound). Music is transcoded to MP3 at import.
- Video: the Bink WASM decoder is used only for the main-menu video (ra2ts_l.bik).

feature_completeness:
"Code" means verified in code; "README" means claimed only.

**Present:**
- Skirmish vs AI: code. SkirmishScreen and LobbyType.Singleplayer. The bot is Supalosa's bot (7,367 lines) extended to about 12.1k lines under game/ai. It parses retail aimd.ini TaskForces and AITriggerTypes, has difficulty levels, personalities and a superweapon officer. AI quality is claimed to be good, and there are soak/qualification tests on beta, but I did not verify it in play.
- RA2 and Yuri's Revenge factions, units and buildings: code. EngineType.YurisRevenge is present, and tests boot both engines. Yuri-specific systems are present (slave miner, grinder, bio reactor, tank bunker, gattling), per commits and code.
- Superweapons: code. game/superweapon/ has ChronoSphere, IronCurtain, Nuke, LightningStorm, PsychicDominator, GeneticConverter, ForceShield, PsychicReveal, SpyPlane, Paradrop, plus Ares extras.
- Naval units, water, bridges, garrisoning, veterancy, fog and shroud: code. There are many files for each (Veteran 105, Bridge 199, Occupy/Garrison 54, Shroud 70, naval 30), MapShroudLayer exists, and debug:minimap-shroud is a test flow.
- LAN multiplayer: code, via WebRTC with manual SDP/QR (network/lan/*) and lockstep, plus debug:lan-* flows.
- Custom maps: code, partial. Engine.supportedMapTypes = ["mpr","map"], so .yrm is not listed. There is also a map-transfer flow for LAN.
- Sound, EVA voices and music: code (engine/sound Eva, Music, Mixer). Music is transcoded to MP3 at import.
- Save/load: code, partial. GameScreen.saveGame stores a replay checkpoint ("[SAVE] … min"), and LoadGameScreen resumes single-player games from it.
- Replays: code (ReplayRecorder, ReplayScreen).
- INI-driven modding: code. The rules/art/ai INIs are read from the user's MIXes, CD-style *cd.ini overrides exist, and there is a Mods menu (mods.ini) plus an Ares data-driven layer (docs/AresCompatibilityMatrix.md). Mental Omega is explicitly "not claimed complete".
- Performance at high resolution: partly code. Native device-pixel rendering, a thermal pass, fitted shadow maps and a merged terrain mesh are present. Performance was not measured on this machine.

**Missing:**
- Allied, Soviet and YR campaigns: MISSING (code). There is no campaign UI. VirtualFileSystem.isCampaignOnlyMixFilename deliberately skips movie and mission MIXes because "Campaign presentation/content is deliberately outside the current boot contract". Triggers are a subset: 39 conditions and 44 executors. There is no map TeamType, ScriptType or reinforcement execution.
- Online multiplayer: MISSING. servers.ini endpoints are blank, with the note "Play online at https://chronodivide.com instead".
- FMV cutscenes: MISSING, since there is no campaign. Only the main-menu Bink video plays, via the WASM decoder.
- Map editor: MISSING (no code found).
- Weather: MISSING. There is no rain or snow system; only lightning-storm flashes exist.

**Platforms:** Tauri desktop, Android and iOS shells exist in code. Releases for them are claimed in the README but do not exist.
asset_requirements:
VERIFIED in code:
- The user supplies a retail RA2 install, optionally with YR (the README points to Steam app 2229850). Nothing is bundled.
- For RA2, the importer requires ra2.mix, language.mix and multi.mix (GameResImporter.REQUIRED_ROOT_MIXES). theme.mix is optional and is transcoded to MP3.
- For YR, GameProfile also requires ra2md.mix, langmd.mix and multimd.mix. The expandmd##/ecache##/elocal## MIXes are copied, and thememd.mix is converted.
- Loaded internally from inside ra2.mix and the other archives: local.mix, isosnow/isotemp/isourb, snow/temperat/urban, sidec01/02, anims, vxl, cameo and others (engine/resourceConfigs.ts).
- There are two ways to supply the files:
  - In the browser or app: Menu import. The user picks a folder, archive or zip (File System Access / Tauri dialog / 7z-wasm), and the importer splits and transcodes into OPFS.
  - For development: `./scripts/setup.sh "/path/to/Red Alert 2"`, which runs scripts/prepare-gameres.ts. It writes the gitignored gameres-export/ plus general.csf/generalmd.csf, extracted from language.mix/langmd.mix, into redalert2/public.
- Mental Omega and other mods are imported as folders or archives and selected in Menu → Mods.
- The repo still ships Chrono Divide-authored small files in public/res (rulescd.ini, artcd.ini, mpmodescd.ini, missions.pkt with "Fixes for vanilla maps"). ra2cd.mix was later removed by 32c470e ("Package engine without bundled game archives").
hd_extensibility:
Paths are under redalert2/src/. Difficulty is my estimate.

**Overall architecture:** good. The simulation (game/) never imports the renderer. The renderer subscribes to game events (for example WarheadDetonateFxHandler subscribes to EventType), so rendering can be replaced without touching determinism.

**1) Hi-res sprite replacement (SHP) — Medium**
- Hook points: ImageFinder.ts (resolves art to ShpFile) and renderable/builder/ShpTextureAtlas.fromShpFile / ShpBuilder.useMaterial.
- ShpBuilder.useMaterial currently throws unless the texture format is RedFormat.
- Add an HD override lookup keyed by image name and frame. It would load 2×/4× RGBA atlases plus a house-color mask channel standing in for remap indices 16–31, and a new RGBA material variant beside PaletteBasicMaterial.
- Sprite geometry size is in world units (SpriteUtils.createSpriteGeometry scale / Coords.ISO_WORLD_SCALE), so higher texel density needs no geometry change.
- Batching (BatchShpBuilder, MergedSpriteMesh, InstancedMesh) assumes shared R8 atlases and palette rows, so batching needs parallel RGBA atlases.

**2) Terrain (TMP) — Medium to hard**
- engine/renderable/entity/map/MapTileLayer.createTileObjects merges all tiles into one mesh with an R8 atlas and the iso palette, with per-tile light in vertexColorMult.
- Swap TmpDrawable → TextureAtlas for an HD RGBA/normal atlas (or a material-splat terrain) while keeping the per-tile geometry and lighting attribute.
- Ramps and "extra data" (hasExtraData offsets) complicate things.

**3) Voxel upgrade — Easy to medium; the best part of this codebase**
- Voxels are already real meshes: renderable/builder/vxlGeometry/VxlGeometryMonotoneBuilder.ts plus VxlBuilder, VxlNonBatchedBuilder and VxlBatchedBuilder, with HVA per-section transforms.
- Options: smooth the VXL meshes (surface nets or marching cubes, plus normal smoothing), or substitute authored glTF models per section, and swap PalettePhongMaterial for MeshStandardMaterial/PBR with a team-color mask.
- Shadows already work through WorldScene's DirectionalLight shadow map.
- Fix Renderer.supportsInstancing (it checks the WebGL1-only ANGLE_instanced_arrays) to re-enable batching.

**4) Normal and depth-map lighting for sprites — Hard**
- Needs a new sprite material that samples normal and depth maps, and a lights buffer from Lighting.ts / LightingDirector.ts / ExtraLightHelper.
- Everything is currently computed in "palette byte domain" (paletteShaderLib comments), so a linear-space lighting path has to be added in parallel.

**5) Post-processing — Easy to medium**
- Insert an EffectComposer or render target for the world scene only in engine/gfx/Renderer.render(), which loops scenes and calls renderer.render per viewport. UiScene stays un-post-processed.
- Caveat noted in code: palette materials write display-referred values and would be wrong inside a WebGLRenderTarget. That needs an explicit colorspace fix: an sRGB target, or an encode in the final pass.
- Candidate effects: bloom, SSAO/AO on voxels, color grading, TAA/SMAA, DOF tilt-shift.

**6) Water shader — Medium to hard**
- Nothing exists today; water is plain TMP tiles.
- Detect LandType.Water tiles in MapTileLayer, exclude them from the merged mesh, and add a WaterLayer renderable (flow normals, planar or SSR-style reflection of the ortho scene, shoreline foam from tile adjacency).
- Hook ship wakes via entity/plugin/ShipWakeTrailPlugin.ts.

**7) Weather — Medium**
- Add a WeatherLayer to WorldScene or MapRenderable: GPU-instanced rain or snow, wet-ground darkening via a Lighting.ts ambient tweak, and fog through a post pass.
- The existing hooks are LightingDirector plus the LightningStormFx pattern, and the map [Lighting] section and trigger executors SetAmbient*.

**8) GPU particles and modern hit effects — Medium**
- Replace the outdated shader-particle-engine 1.0.6 (fx/speRuntime.ts, speCompat.ts, which need a THREE global) used by DamageSmokeFx, TrailerSmokeFx and SparkFx with a modern instanced or TSL particle system.
- Augment explosion SHP anims in fx/handler/WarheadDetonateFxHandler.ts and RenderableManager.createTransientAnim with volumetric sprites, shockwaves, debris (entity/Debris.ts) and screen shake, keyed by warhead or anim name.

**9) WebGPU — Hard**
- three r183 ships WebGPURenderer, but every custom material patches GLSL ShaderChunks (PaletteBasic/Lambert/Phong via string replace). All of them would have to be rewritten in TSL.
- Staying on WebGL2 is fine for a 2.5D HD target.
risks: LICENSING (critical): The roughly 127k-line engine core is, by its own upstream's admission, 'code reconstructed from the Chrono Divide client'. On 2026-09-03 huangkaoya replaced GPL-3.0 with a notice that Chrono Divide-derived material 'is not licensed under GPL-3.0 or any other open-source license'. StillM8's GPL-3.0 declaration therefore has no valid grant behind it for most of the code, and its own THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES admits the repo 'comes down' if the author objects. Any public or commercial HD remaster built on it is exposed to a takedown by Chrono Divide's author (Alexandru Ciucă), in addition to EA trademark and asset issues.
The skirmish AI is derived from Supalosa's bot, which has no license (license null, 'UNLICENSED'). Beyond the lack of a grant, this is the AI a skirmish-first remaster would depend on.

Git history contains EA retail data (public/ini.mix with rules/art/ai INIs, and Westwood files in ra2cd.mix, removed later in cf899d4, fca65f8 and 32c470e). A fork carries it unless history is rewritten.

No campaign support at all: campaign MIXes are deliberately excluded, only 44 of the ~140 RA2 trigger actions are implemented, and there are no TeamTypes, ScriptTypes, reinforcements, briefings or cutscenes. Step 1 ('original functionality') would require building the whole campaign layer.
No online multiplayer (endpoints blank) and no map editor. .yrm maps are not in supportedMapTypes.

Single maintainer with AI-agent burst development (170 commits in one day). The stable branch main fails its own typecheck with 68 errors, and most of the work is split across beta and ai/* branches. There are 0 releases despite the README's download table, and the project has 1 star and 0 forks, so bus-factor and continuity risk is high.

Reconstructed code quality: heavy use of `any`, residual minifier parameter names (e, t), leftover debug console.log in hot paths (MapTileLayer), and a dated particle library that needs a THREE global.
Instancing is probably silently disabled on WebGL2 (the WebGL1 ANGLE_instanced_arrays check in Renderer.supportsInstancing). This is inference: I did not run it in a browser.
The palette-byte-domain shading pipeline makes linear-space HD lighting and post-processing (render targets) non-trivial, and the code itself warns about this.
score_rationale:
Technically, this is one of the strongest candidates in the Chrono Divide family. It builds cleanly (beta: typecheck clean, 858 tests passing), RA2 + YR skirmish is broad (superweapons, garrisons, naval, veterancy, a strong ai.ini-driven bot), LAN, save/load and replays work in code, and the renderer is a real Three.js r183 3D scene with an isometric orthographic camera. Mesh voxels with shadow maps, a clean sim/render split and event-driven FX make the 2.5D HD upgrades (post-processing, voxel meshes, particles, water, weather) quite feasible; I'd rate it about 7–8/10 for renderer upgradability alone.

The weighted score is pulled down hard by three things:
- Legality, about 1/10. The code is an unlicensed reconstruction of a proprietary client. Upstream explicitly disclaimed GPL on 2026-09-03, and the AI is unlicensed too. That makes it acceptable only for private, non-commercial tinkering, with takedown risk for anything published.
- Original-functionality completeness. There are no Allied, Soviet or YR campaigns, no FMV cutscenes, no online play and no map editor. That is a big gap for 'restore the original game first'.
- Maintenance. A single AI-driven maintainer, 1 star, no releases, and a main branch that fails typecheck.

On balance it is a good technical prototype and reference, but a weak legal foundation for a remaster: 4/10. If the user accepts a strictly private, non-distributed project, the beta branch is a practical starting point. Otherwise, prefer a clean-licensed base such as OpenRA-based RA2, or independent code, and use this repo only as an architectural reference, without copying its code.
